Limits acceptance on quantized targets: quantization reduces precision of target model weights/activations, causing logit distribution shifts, especially for low-bit quantization, leading to more mismatches between draft and target. Also target may be quantized for memory/throughput, but acceptance depends on target's output distribution. Quantization noise changes probabilities, top-k/top-p, temperature, and can make target less deterministic; if target uses quantized logits, draft trained on full precision may mismatch. Also quantization can degrade target quality, but acceptance is about agreement. How speculative decoding works:
- Standard autoregressive LLM generates token by token, each token requires full forward pass.
- Speculative decoding uses small fast draft model to propose sequence of K tokens (speculative tokens) given prefix.
- Target model evaluates all proposed tokens in one batched forward pass (or parallel positions) and produces logits for each position.
- Compare draft tokens to target's sampled/argmax tokens. Accept longest prefix where they match. If mismatch at position i, discard proposed tokens from i onward, keep accepted prefix, and continue drafting from there.
- If all K accepted, repeat. If none accepted, still target produced one token (or maybe fallback). Speedup = (K+1)/A? Actually target forward passes per accepted token = 1/(acceptance length) maybe. Need mention latency vs throughput.
- Requirements: draft and target must be compatible, target can batch draft tokens, KV cache. Acceptance rate depends on draft quality, target entropy, sampling settings.
